summary: The 503 number is real and mostly honest: I ran the full suite once (503 passed, 136.94s) and sampled ~12 files across auth, 2FA, extension, llm, study tools, payments/trial, library and security. The suite asserts on real behaviour (status+body, numeric token/credit balances, actual wire-model slugs, clamped coordinates), not string-grep proxies. But the number falsely reassures in three places: (1) the trash restore/purge lifecycle in server/trash.py — the only safety net on every delete button — has ZERO test; (2) CSRF enforcement's rejection branch is never exercised because every test authenticates with a Bearer header, which csrf.py exempts at line 84-85; (3) the extension's CDP/debugger element collection (the load-bearing 'live DOM registry' path) is client-side MV3 JS and untestable by pytest. The 'known red' test is now green at HEAD (verified 3x isolated + full file + full suite). The prior production-safety finding (suite booting the prod lifespan janitor) is FIXED in conftest.py. I could not check whether GitHub Actions actually runs/passes (no GH access from this box).

findings.title: Trash restore/purge lifecycle has zero test coverage
findings.evidence: server/trash.py is 148 lines (move_to_trash, restore, purge_expired, RETENTION_DAYS=10, RESTORE_HANDLERS) and is imported by exactly 0 test files. `grep -rln 'server.trash|move_to_trash' server/tests/ tests/` returns nothing. routes_library.py:139-140 calls move_to_trash() on every DELETE, yet test_library_v3.py:70-72 only asserts `del_res.json()['status'] == 'ok'` — it never asserts a TrashItem row was created, that restore() re-inserts the StudyMaterial, or that purge_expired() removes items past expires_at.
findings.impact: The only thing standing between a user's delete and permanent data loss is an untested module. If restore() or purge_expired() silently broke (e.g. a schema mismatch, a bad handler lookup at trash.py:136), all 503 tests would still pass and users would lose work with no way back.
findings.verified_how: grep for 'trash' across server/tests/ + tests/ = 0 source-file matches (only .pyc noise); read server/trash.py and test_library_v3.py in full.

findings.title: CSRF rejection branch is never exercised — every test bypasses it via Bearer
findings.evidence: server/csrf.py:84-85 `if request.headers.get('Authorization', '').startswith('Bearer '): return` exempts all Bearer requests. conftest.py:130-150 issues a JWT Bearer for every authenticated test. The 403 rejection (`raise HTTPException(403, 'CSRF token missing/invalid')` at csrf.py:94-99) only fires for cookie-authenticated (helpotron_session) mutations, and no test posts such a request WITHOUT a valid X-CSRF-Token and asserts 403. The 2FA purchase tests (test_auth_2fa.py:151-203) do use cookie auth but always send a valid token.
findings.impact: A security control that is not tested is unenforced by default. If validate_csrf() silently stopped raising (e.g. a typo'd constant, a bad path-exempt condition), the entire suite would still pass green and cookie-authenticated state-changing requests would be CSRF-unprotected in production.
findings.verified_how: Read server/csrf.py; grep 'X-CSRF|cookies|helpotron_session' across tests — the only cookie-auth tests are the 2FA purchase flow, which always attach a valid token.

findings.title: Extension CDP/debugger element collection is untestable by the pytest suite
findings.evidence: The 'live DOM element registry' collection lives entirely in extension/agent_mode.js (chrome.debugger.attach at :697, Runtime.evaluate element-geometry extraction at :723 and :767). server/tests/test_extension_live_elements.py only tests the server-side string formatter _render_live_elements (routes_extension.py), never the collection itself. 0 Python tests touch chrome.debugger/CDP.
findings.impact: The load-bearing path that tells the model what it can click/see on a live page has no automated verification anywhere in the 503. A coordinate-space or shadow-DOM regression in the collection would ship undetected (several such bugs are already in git log: fd31f75, 6d3ff1b, 94c9e2d).
findings.verified_how: Read agent_mode.js CDP section and test_extension_live_elements.py; grep 'chrome.debugger|Runtime.evaluate|cdp' in server/tests/ = 0 meaningful matches.

findings.title: The 'known red' test now passes at HEAD — CONTEXT claim is stale
findings.evidence: server/tests/test_extension_agent_chat.py::test_browser_search_with_math_query_never_intercepted_by_shell passed 3/3 isolated runs and 10/10 in its file; full suite = 503 passed at HEAD 304542e. The test asserts _extract_shell_query(t1)=='' (lines 183-184) and the route returns real control_actions, and routes_overlord.py:1358 `if _BROWSER_INTENT_PAT.search(text): return ''` is the code that satisfies it.
findings.impact: Both TEST and CODE are correct at HEAD — the regression is genuinely fixed and the test is a valid guard, not a proxy. The finding is informational: the sweep brief's 'fails at HEAD' is no longer true, so no red-test remediation is needed.
findings.verified_how: pytest -q on the single test (3x), the whole file, and one full-suite run (503 passed, 2:16).

findings.title: Shared persistent test DB + fixed-name users = order/state-dependent risk
findings.evidence: conftest.py:6 pins DATABASE_URL to `sqlite:///./test_helpotron.db` (a persistent file, not a tempfile); init_db() (server/database.py:659-660) uses create_all, never drop_all. Tests use both uuid users AND fixed public_ids ('nuclear_student', 'sec_pw_user', 'test_purchase_user_2fa', 'test_lib_user'). test_extension_releases.py:42 comment admits 'Shared session-scoped test DB persists between runs' and relies on manual self-purge.
findings.impact: A test is only a test if it passes from any prior state. A leftover row from a failed/interrupted run (or a fixed-name user seeded by a different test) can flip an assertion's outcome — exactly the misdiagnosed-flake class the sweep is hunting. The suite is green today only because it happens to self-clean the rows it depends on.
findings.verified_how: Read conftest.py, database.py init_db, and test_extension_releases.py; grep for fixed-name public_ids in tests.

findings.title: The streak timezone fix is not locked by a test
findings.evidence: routes_study_tools.py:268-273 documents the UTC/local bug (now fixed to `datetime.now(timezone.utc).date()`), but the only streak assertion is test_study_tools_v3.py:99 `assert s_data['streak_days'] >= 1` against a freshly-created session. No test forces a UTC-midnight boundary (e.g. created_at=23:30Z, local=next-day) to pin the fix.
findings.impact: The bug that 'cost days to diagnose' will return un-noticed the next time someone swaps the date source, because the loose >=1 assertion passes on the happy path either way. (Good news: grep found no OTHER naive date.today()/datetime.now() in server/*.py — only utcnow/timezone.utc plus one intentional date-query string at routes_overlord.py:1336.)
findings.verified_how: Read routes_study_tools.py:244-296 and test_study_tools_v3.py:90-100; grep for naive datetime usage across server/*.py.

fixes.change: Add assertions after the DELETE: query TrashItem for the user, assert one row exists with item_type='study_material' and correct payload.id; then call server.trash.restore() and assert the StudyMaterial row is re-inserted; then set expires_at in the past, call purge_expired(), and assert the row is gone. Cover the 'no restore handler' negative (trash.py:136-138).
fixes.verify: .venv/bin/python -m pytest server/tests/test_library_v3.py -q  (expect new tests green and 503+2 collected)
fixes.risk: None — additive assertions on the isolated test DB.

fixes.change: Add a test: sign up+login to obtain the helpotron_session + csrf_token cookies, then POST a state-changing route (e.g. /api/assignments) with cookies but NO X-CSRF-Token header and assert 403; then repeat WITH the matching token and assert it succeeds. This exercises csrf.py:94-99.
fixes.risk: None — additive; must use a route not in csrf.py EXEMPT_PATHS.

fixes.change: Point DATABASE_URL at a per-run temp SQLite file (tempfile.mkdtemp) instead of ./test_helpotron.db, and drop_all/create_all in the session fixture before init_db(), so every run starts from an empty schema.
fixes.verify: Run the suite twice back-to-back with no cleanup; assert identical pass count.
fixes.risk: Tests relying on cross-test seeded rows (fixed-name users) would need to seed their own fixtures — a one-time refactor of ~5 files.

verification_plan: 1. .venv/bin/python -m pytest server/tests/ -q  -> expect 503 passed (reconfirms the headline number).
2. grep -rn 'trash' server/tests/ tests/  -> expect 0 source-file matches (confirms S7-1).
3. grep -rn 'helpotron_session' server/tests/ and grep -rn 'X-CSRF' server/tests/  -> confirm no negative CSRF assertion exists (confirms S7-2).
5. Read server/csrf.py:84-85 and conftest.py:130-150 to confirm every authenticated test uses Bearer.
6. Read server/trash.py and test_library_v3.py:70-72 to confirm the delete test never touches trash.
